recent_cases.parties: Fotu v Minister for Immigration and Citizenship
recent_cases.ai_summary: The Minister used s 501BA(2) of the Migration Act to overturn an Administrative Review Tribunal decision and cancel the applicant's visa on national interest grounds. The Federal Court upheld the first ground of judicial review, finding the Minister's reasoning and dismissal of the Tribunal's approach to assessing the risk of reoffending was illogical and revealed jurisdictional error. The Court rejected the remaining grounds concerning consideration of the interests of minor relatives and the legal consequences of immigration detention, and quashed the Minister's decision.

recent_cases.parties: Kola v Minister for Immigration and Citizenship
recent_cases.ai_summary: The applicant sought judicial review of an Administrative Review Tribunal decision refusing his citizenship application under s 21(2)(h) of the Australian Citizenship Act 2007 (Cth) because it was not satisfied he was of good character given his criminal history. The applicant argued the Tribunal was legally unreasonable, denied procedural fairness by giving reduced weight to character witness statements whose authors were not cross-examined, and misapplied the good character test by letting his offending outweigh rehabilitation evidence. The Federal Court dismissed the appeal, finding no jurisdictional error.

recent_cases.parties: Vanu v Minister for Immigration and Citizenship
recent_cases.ai_summary: The applicant sought an urgent interlocutory injunction to prevent his removal from Australia to New Zealand after the Administrative Review Tribunal affirmed a decision not to revoke the cancellation of his visa. The Court found no serious question to be tried on the application for an extension of time to seek judicial review and that the balance of convenience did not favour an injunction. The interlocutory application was refused.

recent_cases.parties: DXJL and Minister for Immigration and Citizenship (Migration)
recent_cases.ai_summary: The Tribunal reviewed a delegate's decision not to revoke the mandatory cancellation of the applicant's Global Special Humanitarian (Subclass 202) visa. The applicant did not pass the character test, and the Tribunal weighed the Direction 110 considerations, finding that community protection and community expectations outweighed his ties to Australia and the best interests of minor children. The Tribunal affirmed the non-revocation decision.

recent_cases.parties: Rahimi and Minister for Immigration and Citizenship (Migration)
recent_cases.ai_summary: The applicant, a Class XB Subclass 201 (In Country Special Humanitarian) visa holder, had his visa cancelled under s 501(3A) after failing the character test. On review, the Tribunal weighed the Direction No 110 considerations, finding that although protection of the community and community expectations weighed against revocation, the applicant's ties to Australia, the legal consequences of removal to Afghanistan, and extreme impediments faced there outweighed those factors, particularly given his mental illness and treatment. The Tribunal set aside the cancellation decision and substituted a decision to revoke the cancellation under s 501CA(4).
